html:
The Macedonian independence referendum was held on 8 September 1991, and voters chose independence from Yugoslavia by a large majority, though much of the Albanian minority boycotted it.

Macedonia was the only republic to leave Yugoslavia without war: the Yugoslav army withdrew peacefully in 1992. But Greece objected to the name Macedonia, which it saw as a claim on its own northern province and on Alexander the Great. The country joined the United Nations in 1993 under the temporary name Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, and Greece imposed a trade embargo. Tensions with the Albanian minority led to the conflict of 2001, and the name dispute lasted until the Prespa Agreement of 2018.
sum: The Macedonian independence referendum was held on 8 September 1991, and voters chose independence from Yugoslavia by a large majority, though much of the Albanian minority boycotted it.
